newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 26.

text.p: Morgan uses relative's home as court surety: Big-spending NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan has offered his mother-in-law's house as security to cover legal costs should he lose his defamation action against Labour MP Trevor Mallard. Page 1.

South Island pays true cost of power says Bradford: Energy Minister Max Bradford signalled little support on Wednesday for those favouring retaining the South Island electricity differential, saying the lower prices in the South Island already reflected lower transmission costs there. Page 2.

Benefits can be cut sooner under new change: Parliament on Wednesday night passed legislation allowing the Social Welfare Department to act more quickly against beneficiaries who failed to attend interviews or turned down suitable jobs. Page 2.

INP cool on TeNZ shares: The Stock Exchange's TeNZ fund put 590,000 Wilson and Horton shares up for sale on Wednesday, but the company's majority owners have shown no interest in the parcel so far. Page 13.

Sexism rife in judicial system: Report reveals bias against women judges: New Zealand's judicial system is riddled with sexism -- from the benches of top judges down to the lawyers who stand before them.

New pessimism puts pressure on Peters: The urgency of the challenge confronting the Treasurer, Winston Peters, in today's budget has become even more pressing with the release of further evidence of a dramatic slump in business confidence.
Fletcher newsprint buyout approved: Fletcher Challenge Paper has been cleared by Australia's monopolies watchdog to buy the half share of Australian Newsprint Mills it doesn't already own.
Countrywide renewing system for 2000: Countrywide Bank has embarked on a total revamp of its information technology systems that will cost "tens of millions" of dollars over the next three years.

Pay of directors trails way behind Australia: Chairmen and directors of New Zealand companies are paid much less than their Australian counterparts, according to the 1997 transtasman annual board of directors study by consultants Korn/Ferry International.

Issue shortfall costs Brierley: Brierley Investments is expected to forgo $30 million in profit from Weeks Bass Strait Royalty after an issue of units in the Australian oil and gas fields fell 25 percent short.
Business confidence key to Budget: Winston Peters will seek to restore business confidence and the coalition's standing in the Budget he will deliver this afternoon. Page 1.

Judge to study MP's allegations: Retired youth court judge Mick Brown will look into allegations that Auckland child-welfare staff falsified documents, Social Welfare Minister Roger Sowry said on Wednesday. Page 5.
